task_objective: Restrict BLOCK to deterministic structural artifact facts and rank the review queue by inverse corpus rule frequency without changing classifications.

setup.plan_state: The plan was already committed as the tip of dev and therefore became the implementation branch point; no duplicate empty plan commit was created.
setup.remote_dev_pull: Attempted git pull --ff-only origin dev; origin has no dev ref. The clean local dev commit 733afb5 was used as the required base.
setup.incident_before_change: A direct SHELL_CURL_PIPE fixture produced one finding classified BLOCK and an aggregate release classification of BLOCK.

policy_decisions.archive_duplicate_path: Excluded from blockable_rules and retained as MANUAL_REVIEW because the audited corpus contains a legitimate normalized-path collision.
policy_decisions.corrupt_archive: Excluded from blockable_rules because it means inspection could not complete; required scanner failures preserve AUDIT_ERROR rather than treating corruption as proof of maliciousness.
policy_decisions.precedence: rule_classifications overrides run first, then the blockable_rules ceiling is applied. Overrides may demote a structural rule, but cannot promote a non-structural rule above MANUAL_REVIEW.
policy_decisions.rarity_storage: Rarity is computed from the verdict store at report time and is not persisted. Persisting a corpus-relative score would require rewriting unchanged records whenever N or a rule frequency changes.
policy_decisions.test_expectation_changes: Legacy expectations that behavioural secret and incident rules remained BLOCK were changed because the plan explicitly replaces that contract; findings and rule IDs remain present.

implementation: Policy loading validates blockable_rules as a list of known rule IDs and rejects unknown IDs.
One central policy application function applies per-rule overrides and then caps every non-blockable BLOCK finding at MANUAL_REVIEW.
The review queue sums log(N / frequency) once per distinct rule ID per release, sorts deterministically, and reports the top ten releases with their three rarest contributing rules.
The README now names every structural BLOCK category and states that behavioural findings inform review but never remove a plugin.

verification_evidence.targeted_green: 10 dedicated tests passed; combined auditor coverage passed with 191 tests and 7 subtests.
verification_evidence.structural_controls: Path traversal, setuid archive member, and a simulated ClamAV signature each remained BLOCK.
verification_evidence.policy_errors_and_precedence: A typoed blockable ID raised ValueError; a structural override to PASS_WITH_WARNINGS won, while an explicit behavioural BLOCK override was capped at MANUAL_REVIEW.
verification_evidence.rarity_non_gating: Ranking left every input classification and the verdict-store bytes unchanged; rarity_score is absent from all 42 records.
verification_evidence.mutation: With the central cap removed, the incident negative control failed BLOCK != MANUAL_REVIEW while the archive and ClamAV structural controls passed: 1 failed, 2 passed.
verification_evidence.quality_gates: ruff clean; ruff format clean; 274 passed and 21 subtests passed in 1.30s; no deleted review notes; quality gates passed.

explicitly_not_verified: The structural rules have not fired on this corpus, so their true-positive rate remains unmeasured.
Rarity ranking inherits false-positive findings and prioritizes review rather than proving maliciousness.
Re-enabling enforcement and auditing inherited upstream catalog plugins remain out of scope.
